text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 4.5% today as geopolitical tension in the Middle East escalated sharply—Iran attacked U.S. military sites in Kuwait and struck a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, while a third U.S. carrier deployed to the Gulf. Despite these supply-risk headlines, U.S. crude fell to $89.62 a barrel, and refineries are running at high capacity (95.2%) with ample fuel inventories, limiting the upside benefit that Middle East turmoil might otherwise provide to refiner profits.

The sell-off fits a broader two-week decline of 3.8%, suggesting investors are pricing in weaker refining margins ahead—even as the IEA warns the Strait of Hormuz is no longer a reliable corridor, the actual crude and product prices don't yet reflect a major disruption, leaving refiners stuck between headlines of conflict and market prices that haven't moved decisively in their favor.
